snapshot_purpose: A fixed, reviewable 13 September 2026 thesis for the Copom/FOMC week. It separates the dollar-positive rate signal from the real-positive oil-export signal and waits for price confirmation.

source_failures: CME FedWatch live refresh failed during the final audit because the official interactive tool returned HTTP/2 protocol errors and then timed out. The previously verified 1 September 02:07:02 CT values are retained and explicitly flagged as stale.
refresh_status.note: BCB and FRED observations were refreshed on 13 September. The thesis uses the latest validated official observations while retaining the dated 1 September B3 and CME meeting-pricing anchors, which are explicitly marked as stale.

scenario_axis: The labels describe Brazil's monetary stance relative to the US and to the current exchange-pricing anchors saved below, not a claim that both central banks move in the same hawkish or dovish direction.

scenario_label_audit.result: The three scenario labels are retained, but the 1 September B3 and CME observations are now treated only as dated anchors. The updated thesis therefore relies on current official rates, FX and commodity observations plus price confirmation—not on a claim about live meeting probabilities.
scenario_label_audit.probability_policy: Only CME's published FOMC probabilities are reported. No Copom probability or joint probability is assigned.

fomc.methodology: CME FedWatch converts 30-Day Federal Funds futures prices into target-range probabilities for the selected FOMC meeting. The values are copied from the official tool's 16 September 2026 view.
fomc.staleness_note: CME labels the saved observation 'Data as of 1 Sep 2026 02:07:02 CT.' A final refresh attempt at 21:40 Brasilia time failed because the official interactive tool returned HTTP/2 errors and timed out, so these probabilities may have changed.

copom.source: B3 BVBG.187.01 Simplified Price Report - Derivatives
copom.methodology: The DI1V26 rate is recovered from B3's settlement unit price using rate = (100000 / PU)^(252 / business_days) - 1. DI1U26 matured on 1 September, so B3's published 13.900% adjusted-quote rate is used as the pre-decision anchor. DI1V26 is split into 10 business days before and 11 business days after the 16 September decision; geometric compounding solves the post-meeting rate.
copom.interpretation: The curve embeds about 21.8 bp of easing across the Copom window, which is consistent with most of a 25 bp cut being priced. This is a transparent curve decomposition, not a B3-published Copom probability.
copom.staleness_note: The 1 September report was the latest completed B3 settlement file at the final audit and was published at 20:35 Brasilia time. The decomposition ignores term premia and assumes no other rate change inside the contract window.

entry_trigger.calculation: Round the saved 20-observation range high to two decimals.

invalidation_reference.calculation: Round the saved 20-observation range midpoint to two decimals.

measured_move_review_zone.calculation: Add one unrounded saved range width to the unrounded saved range high, then bracket the result to the adjacent lower and upper cents.

fomc_september_2026.status: scheduled; meeting includes a Summary of Economic Projections

copom_latest.decision: Copom unanimously reduced the Selic target by 0.25 percentage point, from 14.25% to 14.00% p.a.
copom_latest.statement_summary: The statement described gradual moderation in activity, still-elevated inflation and expectations above target, and said the calibration cycle would be adjusted with incoming data while policy remained contractionary.
copom_latest.minutes_summary: The minutes said evidence of restrictive-policy transmission was accumulating, but demand-driven inflation and asymmetric upside risks still required tight policy, cautious calibration and readiness to react to second-round effects.
copom_latest.staleness_note: These were the latest Copom statement and minutes available at retrieval.

fomc_latest.decision: The FOMC maintained the federal-funds target range at 3.50%-3.75% by a 9-3 vote; three voters preferred a 0.25 percentage-point increase.
fomc_latest.statement_summary: The statement said activity was expanding at a solid pace, inflation remained elevated relative to 2%, and the Committee would deliver price stability.
fomc_latest.minutes_summary: Most participants supported holding, several favored a 0.25 percentage-point increase, and the minutes recorded that market pricing at the July meeting implied a September increase; that pricing observation is historical, not a current probability estimate.
fomc_latest.staleness_note: These were the latest FOMC statement and minutes available. The minutes' description of market pricing refers to conditions around 29 July; current 1 September CME pricing is recorded separately in scenario_label_audit.

scenarios.name: Hawkish relative to expectations
scenarios.copom_outcome_and_guidance: Copom holds the Selic target at 14.00% and emphasizes that further easing requires clearer re-anchoring, keeping an explicitly restrictive and data-dependent bias.
scenarios.fomc_outcome_and_guidance: The FOMC holds 3.50%-3.75% rather than hiking, but retains firm price-stability language and optionality to tighten later.
scenarios.difference_from_current_expectations: The Copom hold is hawkish to the B3 curve's roughly 21.8 bp of September easing; the FOMC hold is dovish to CME FedWatch's saved 68.2% weight on a 0.25 pp hike. Together they leave Brazil's relative carry 0.50 pp wider than in the base-case path.
scenarios.expected_initial_brl_usd_direction: Likely initial BRL strengthening (USD/BRL lower), all else equal, because the local hold preserves carry while the Fed does not deliver the described hike; broader risk sentiment can dominate.
scenarios.expected_initial_brazil_front_end_rates_: Likely initial upward pressure on Brazil's front-end rates as near-term easing is removed from the path.
scenarios.expected_initial_us_2y_direction: Likely initial downward pressure on the US 2-year yield if the no-hike decision is not offset by stronger guidance.
scenarios.expected_brazil_us_differential_change: Unchanged mechanically near 10.38 pp, which is 0.50 pp wider than the base-case post-meeting differential of about 9.88 pp.
confirmation_signals: The 2026 Focus Selic median revises from 13.75% toward the unchanged 14.00% target.
USD/BRL PTAX breaks below roughly 5.08, the low of the refreshed 20-observation range, while the US 2-year yield falls from 4.56%.
scenarios.principal_risk: A global risk-off or commodity shock could weaken BRL even with a more favorable relative-rate outcome.

scenarios.name: Base case
scenarios.copom_outcome_and_guidance: Copom cuts 0.25 pp to 13.75%, matching the 2026 Focus Selic median, and keeps guidance cautious, restrictive and explicitly dependent on inflation-expectation re-anchoring.
scenarios.fomc_outcome_and_guidance: The FOMC raises the target range 0.25 pp to 3.75%-4.00% and stresses that subsequent decisions depend on incoming inflation and labor data rather than pre-committing to another move.
scenarios.difference_from_current_expectations: A 0.25 pp Copom cut is consistent with the B3 curve embedding roughly 21.8 bp of easing. A 0.25 pp FOMC hike is the highest-weight outcome in the saved CME FedWatch observation at 68.2%; no joint probability is inferred.
scenarios.expected_initial_brl_usd_direction: Likely mild initial BRL depreciation (USD/BRL higher), all else equal, as the policy differential narrows; the reaction may be limited if both decisions are anticipated and is subject to broader risk sentiment.
scenarios.expected_initial_brazil_front_end_rates_: Likely limited downward pressure on Brazil's front-end rates if the cut and cautious guidance validate the existing easing path.
scenarios.expected_initial_us_2y_direction: Likely limited upward pressure on the US 2-year yield; guidance matters because the yield already rose 0.10 pp over the latest five observations.
scenarios.expected_brazil_us_differential_change: Narrows by 0.50 pp, from 10.375 pp to about 9.875 pp, combining a 0.25 pp Copom cut with a 0.25 pp FOMC hike.
confirmation_signals: The official targets move to 13.75% in Brazil and a 3.875% Fed target-range midpoint, producing a differential near 9.88 pp.
USD/BRL PTAX closes above roughly 5.22, the high of the refreshed 20-observation range, while the US 2-year yield remains near or above 4.56%.
scenarios.principal_risk: The paired moves may already be reflected in rates and FX, leaving global risk appetite, commodities or fiscal news as the dominant driver.

scenarios.name: Dovish relative to expectations
scenarios.copom_outcome_and_guidance: Copom cuts 0.50 pp to 13.50% and signals that further gradual easing is possible if inflation expectations continue to improve.
scenarios.fomc_outcome_and_guidance: The FOMC raises the target range 0.25 pp to 3.75%-4.00% and keeps a firmer tightening bias because inflation remains elevated.
scenarios.difference_from_current_expectations: The 0.50 pp Copom cut delivers about 28 bp more easing than the B3 curve embeds and ends below the 2026 Focus Selic median; paired with the CME-aligned US hike, it is more dovish for Brazil versus the US.
scenarios.expected_initial_brl_usd_direction: Likely initial BRL depreciation (USD/BRL higher), all else equal, because the relative-rate differential narrows more sharply; subject to the inflation rationale and global risk sentiment.
scenarios.expected_initial_brazil_front_end_rates_: Likely initial downward pressure on Brazil's front-end rates if the larger cut is viewed as credible rather than premature.
scenarios.expected_initial_us_2y_direction: Likely initial upward pressure on the US 2-year yield under the hike and firmer guidance.
scenarios.expected_brazil_us_differential_change: Narrows by 0.75 pp, from 10.375 pp to about 9.625 pp.
confirmation_signals: The 2026 Focus Selic median revises below 13.75% without a renewed rise in the 2026 IPCA median from 5.0062%.
USD/BRL PTAX clears roughly 5.22 and the US 2-year yield remains above 4.56%.
scenarios.principal_risk: A larger Copom cut could be read as a credibility error, lifting local risk premia and front-end rates rather than producing the assumed orderly easing reaction.

paper_trades.thesis: Rates and oil point in opposite directions. Higher US yields and a potentially smaller Brazil-US rate gap favor the dollar, while oil above USD 100 can support Brazil's export income and the real. USD/BRL near its recent low shows that the dollar case is not yet winning, so the trade requires a confirmed break above 5.22.
supporting_evidence: USD/BRL PTAX fell 0.72% over approximately one month to 5.0915, close to the low of its refreshed 20-observation range.
The US 2-year yield rose 0.31 pp over one month to 4.56%, a dollar-positive signal that USD/BRL has not confirmed.
The current Brazil-US policy differential is 10.375 pp and would narrow by 0.50 pp in the saved base scenario.
Brent reached USD 109.51 per barrel in the latest official observation, supporting Brazilian export income while also increasing global inflation and risk concerns.
paper_trades.catalyst: The 16 September Copom and FOMC decisions and guidance, together with any change in the oil-supply shock or global risk appetite.
paper_trades.entry_logic: No position at the 5.0915 snapshot. Consider the paper trade only after a daily PTAX midpoint closes above approximately 5.22, the rounded high of the refreshed 20-observation range (5.2233), with the US 2-year yield still near or above 4.56% or the policy differential actually narrowing.
paper_trades.invalidation_condition: Before entry, abandon the dollar thesis if PTAX closes below approximately 5.08 while oil remains firm. After entry, invalidate on two consecutive daily midpoints below approximately 5.15, the rounded midpoint of the refreshed range (5.1543), or if the rate gap fails to narrow and export flows continue to support the real.
paper_trades.profit_taking_logic: Add the refreshed 20-observation high (5.2233) to its width (0.1380) to obtain 5.3613; use 5.36-5.37 only as a review zone and reassess sooner if US yields fall or commodity support for the real strengthens.
paper_trades.expected_holding_period: Approximately two to four weeks, spanning the 15-16 September decisions and initial post-meeting repricing.
principal_risks: Oil and other export prices keep bringing dollars into Brazil and support the real.
Copom stays restrictive or the FOMC turns less hawkish, preserving Brazilian carry or lowering US yields.
Brazilian fiscal or election news improves and attracts capital despite the narrower rate gap.
brief_principal_risks: Oil and export income continue to support the real.
Brazil keeps its rate advantage or US yields fall.
Brazilian fiscal or election news attracts capital.
paper_trades.view_change_evidence: Change the view if PTAX closes below 5.08 while oil stays firm, if the Brazil-US rate gap fails to narrow, or if US 2-year yields fall materially from 4.56%. Those outcomes would show that export flows or Brazilian carry matter more than the dollar-positive rate signal.
